meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: The same active site is present in both complexes, so an ATP-competitive inhibitor cannot distinguish them.
data.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 and mTORC2 use the same ATP-binding pocket, so a drug that blocks the pocket hits both and cannot choose. That is thought to explain why this class of drugs causes more metabolic and immune side effects than rapamycin-type drugs, but the size of that effect has only been seen in cell studies and has not been measured in patients.
data.boundary: Explains the metabolic and immunological toxicity of this class relative to rapalogs; the magnitude in patients is not established from these cell-line studies.
